title: Give the worktree-first guard the acting record and the missing no-grant arm
intent: A live incident (beedashboard, 2026-08-12): a session working the hub-finished-compact lane did full feature work in the MAIN checkout and committed to main (c79e071), while the worktree-first guard allowed every write. Two defects: the guard reads state.json (which named a different feature) instead of the session's own lane record, and it only refuses when the feature ALREADY holds a worktree. 78 lane records live across the two repos against 2 default-pipeline state.json records, so the shape the guard cannot see is the dominant one.
action: In packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/hooks/write_guard/: (1) main.rs:325-335 currently passes the raw read_state(store_root) value (main.rs:136) into check_worktree_first, while every other write check goes through resolve_write_record (checks.rs:45-146). Feed check_worktree_first the SAME resolved record — the lane record for a lane-bound session, the default state otherwise. Reuse the resolution already computed for check_write rather than resolving twice; if that value is not in scope at the call site, hoist it. A RecordResolution::Fail must NOT be swallowed into an allow — it already denies upstream, so the worktree-first call simply must not run on a failed resolution. (2) In hook_local.rs check_worktree_first (:510-558), add the arm that is missing at :546-549: when find_feature_worktree_grant returns None for the acting feature, deny instead of allowing, with the remedy `bee worktree new --feature <feature>` — the same command and framing route_worktree_block already prints at state_group/workflows.rs:663-672 ("lane X is code-touching and this is the MAIN checkout — feature work branches at feature start (worktree-first)"). Keep the existing granted-worktree arm's message byte-for-byte. The new arm is narrow and every bound below is load-bearing: it fires ONLY when the acting record's phase is "swarming"; lane "docs" and lane "tiny" never fire (AGENTS.md gives main integration, docs-lane, release work, and a solo tiny fix); a missing or empty route on the acting record stays fail-open (40 of 56 beehive lane records carry no route, and counter-teeth already gave route-less claims their own teeth at cells claim). Every existing carve-out stays byte-for-byte: worktree_first_exempt_rel (.md plus GATE_ALLOWED_PREFIXES), config worktree_first: "off", worktree_resolution != "ordinary", and a corrupt/missing grants registry failing open.
acceptance: A lane-bound session whose lane record names feature F is judged against F, not against the feature state.json names — proven by a fixture built from the live hub-finished-compact.json shape (phase swarming, route.lane small, feature hub-finished-compact) while state.json names a different feature with a different lane.
A code-touching source write in the MAIN checkout at phase swarming, for a feature holding NO granted worktree, is denied and the reason names `bee worktree new --feature <feature>`.
The pre-existing granted-worktree arm still denies with its current message unchanged, including the `bee worktree merge --id <id>` remedy.

No-deny direction proven case by case: lane docs, lane tiny, a phase other than swarming, an acting record with no route, a .md path, a GATE_ALLOWED_PREFIXES path, config worktree_first: "off", a non-ordinary (linked worktree) checkout, and a corrupt grants registry — each allows.

truths: The record check_worktree_first judges is the acting record: for a lane-bound session it is .bee/lanes/<lane>.json, never state.json.
A code-touching main-checkout source write at phase swarming is refused when the acting feature holds no granted worktree, and the refusal names `bee worktree new --feature <feature>`.
The granted-worktree arm's existing refusal text is unchanged.
Each carve-out still allows: lane docs, lane tiny, phase != swarming, no route on the acting record, .md and gate-allowed paths, worktree_first "off", non-ordinary checkout, corrupt grants registry.

trace.outcome: Guard now judges the acting (lane-aware) record and denies a code-touching main-checkout write at phase swarming when the feature holds no granted worktree, naming bee worktree new --feature <feature>; corrupt registry still fails open
